Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0031 html 001b92' (web books meditations13 section0031 html 001b92), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'He respected his own desire for'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0031 html 001b92*, the master explains: *"He respected his own desire for happiness and, through that, he was able to develop qualities of wisdom, purity, compassion."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.
